reason: Measured, not argued: I ran the R2S-2 rule exactly as specified (a copy of trainlab.forkmid with cos>0.25 on FINAL coords, forkmid's drop convention, threshold not tuned) on all 56 exp60 lab dumps with the official scoring (scratch script antipar_lab.py in the session scratchpad; numbers in research/wf_ideas_v4/round2/v_hypotheses_r2s-2.notes.md). The dose reproduces (113/676 = 16.7%, nodes unchanged), but the vetoed evaluable forks are TP 1 / FP 4 / ignored 108 and the pooled div_J falls 0.1290 -> 0.1250 (div TP/FP/FN 16/25/83 -> 15/21/84; score -0.00034; adj_edge +0.00006). The finding's own gate clause 'pooled div_J >= control' FAILS. This is the same failure as forkblob (L4, closed at 20:04 UTC), in the same veto family. It is not a threshold artefact: the vetoed TP (6bba_7f87b3d8, parent 4406) has cos 0.976, so any cos threshold between 0.08 and 0.976 would remove it. In the lab, TP forks show cos>0.25 at 6% (1/16) vs FP forks at 16% (4/25), about 2.6x enrichment. Break-even needs FP:TP >= 1/J, i.e. 7.7:1 at the lab's J of 0.129. The finding's 'FP >= 3*TP' clause and its ~0.0007 value estimate assume a public J of 0.33, and even at 4:1 its q = 0.2 is barely under the 0.25 break-even, with only ~2-3 evaluable public forks, so the result would be noise. Private is other, unseen embryos, and the lab (J ~0.13 on train embryos) is the better proxy there, so the expected value is <= 0. The sign flips between halves (SELECTION -0.0012, CONFIRMATION +0.0006) and between embryos (44b6 +0.0006, 6bba -0.0005), so there is no stable signal. The stacked arm adds nothing: forkmid45+antipar25 is identical to antipar25, because forkmid's single FP removal (6bba_cdcfe533) already falls inside the cos cell. On feasibility the design would be fine (byte-identical off, fail-soft, <1 s per clip, R3 class, fits R8), but it fails its own harm gate. It also needs a user OK that it cannot earn, and it would take agent time from the K2/K3 schedule.
fix: Close R2S-2 (antipar veto) now, with the lab result as the reason. Do not build --patch antipar, do not add a trainlab arm (the evaluation is already done, and adding the arm now would be a post-hoc knob ladder), and do not ask the user for an R3 OK. Record it in the curator IDEAS list as closed next to forkblob: 'post-hoc safe-fork vetoes fail pooled div_J because lab J ~0.13 needs FP:TP >= 7.7'. Keep forkmid on its own L3/T9 audit; its lab result here is 1 FP / 0 TP removed, score +0.00013, so it probably fails L3's FP >= 3. Any future fork veto should state its break-even at the lab J (1/J ~ 7.7), not at the public J.
realistic_gain: Lab: -0.00034 pooled (div_J -0.0040). Public: about 0 +/- 0.001 (2-3 evaluable forks, sign a coin flip). Private: expected <= 0. Nothing to bank.
